clue.text: Not worth considering one legal scholar in casual dress!

indicators.note: in tells us the scholar and the one go inside the item of casual dress

parts.note: a negligee (French négligé) is a loose informal garment
one is the Roman numeral I
BL is Bachelor of Law, a holder of a legal degree

explanation.surface: A lawyer of modest standing turns up dressed down, and nobody pays them any attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and BL inside NEGLIGE, the French spelling of the loose informal garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something negligible is so small or unimportant that it can safely be ignored.

clue.text: Lady at home in Netherlands Antilles

indicators.note: in places the home word within the abbreviation for the islands

parts.note: NA is the abbreviation for the Netherlands Antilles
at home is IN, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A woman is staying at her house in the Caribbean islands once ruled by the Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: Nina is a woman's first name, and crosswords often define a name simply as a lady or girl.

clue.text: This is taken away by Georgia first from gi ant's home

indicators.note: first puts the state's abbreviation at the front of the word that follows

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: taken away means the little word is removed from the larger word

parts.note: the clue's opening word taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is removed by Georgia before it leaves a giant's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken away' removes IS from THIS, leaving TH; 'first' puts GA before it. In the Bible Goliath, the giant slain by David, came from the Philistine city of Gath.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible names the Philistine city of Gath as the hometown of Goliath, the giant David killed.

clue.text: Is king coming up-country?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's legendary British king

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the monarch is heading out of town into the rural parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns LEAR (King Lear) into RAEL in this down clue. 'up-country' looks like one word meaning inland, but the hyphen hides the split.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: In following as a result of it being trivial

parts.note: taken as written

parts.words: following as a result of it
parts.note: consequential means resulting from something, coming as its effect

explanation.surface: A sentence about something minor that follows on from something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without significant consequences is unimportant, the opposite of consequential.

clue.text: Shelter left-winger who looked slyly

parts.note: lee means shelter, as in the lee of a wall
a red is a communist or socialist, a left-winger

explanation.surface: A socialist hiding in a doorway who gave a knowing sideways glance.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone in a sly, knowing or lascivious way.

clue.text: It was considered dangerous to include some Scandinavian books

indicators.note: to include some says part of the preceding words contains the answer

explanation.surface: Certain Nordic volumes were once thought too risky to stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include some' points to letters inside 'considered dangerous': considerED DAngerous.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are two Old Norse works, the Poetic and Prose Edda, collections of Icelandic myth and poetry.

clue.text: Renunciation of the miracles I'd re-enacted

indicators.note: re-enacted means performed again in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes back their claim to have performed wonders that were staged a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-enacted' rearranges the letters of MIRACLES and ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclaimer is a formal denial or renouncing of a claim or responsibility.

clue.text: New play about mother or father it seems

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the family word
new signals the letters of play are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: either a mother or a father is a parent

explanation.surface: A fresh drama about a mum or dad, so it appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges PLAY to APLY, and 'about' wraps AP...LY around PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparently is an adverb meaning seemingly, as far as one can tell.

clue.text: It isn't favourable to be without a game

definitions.meaning: an idiom for conduct that is unfair or unsporting
literally lacking the bat-and-ball game played in England

explanation.surface: Being left with nothing to play is a poor deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for unsporting behaviour, and literally lacking the English bat-and-ball sport.

clue.text: One takes step back at one's earliest convenience

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing

indicators.note: back means the dance word is read in reverse

parts.note: pas is French for step, used in ballet

explanation.surface: Someone retreats a pace whenever it suits them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses PAS (the ballet term for a step) to SAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The initials stand for as soon as possible, a request for prompt action.

clue.text: MPs' joint fraternity?

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament, so members
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Asks whether shared brotherhood unites politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests shared, but it is the body's hip.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraternity is a body of people sharing an interest, as is the membership of a club.

clue.text: Began a journey from Stafford taking in Tel, ford &Eccles first

indicators.note: from here means the answer is made out of these letters reshuffled
first takes the opening letter of each of the two town names

explanation.surface: A trip set out from one Midlands town and called at two others on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives T and E from Telford and Eccles; 'taking in' adds them to STAFFORD, and the ten letters are rearranged. The anagram signal is only the loose 'from', since nothing else marks it.
explanation.definitionFit: To start off is to set out on a trip, to depart.

clue.text: A repairer goes round winding course

indicators.note: goes round means the repairer word surrounds the single letter

parts.note: a mender is someone who repairs things

explanation.surface: A handyman takes a roundabout route to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A meander is a bend in a river, and more generally a twisting path.

clue.text: Small submarine comes up-it carries passengers

parts.note: mini means small

indicators.note: in a down clue, comes up means the word is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A little submarine surfaces carrying its crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' reverses SUB to BUS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A minibus is a small bus for a dozen or so people.

clue.text: One of Yeltsin's compatriots is in great hurry, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: someone in a great hurry is rushing

explanation.surface: A Moscow man dashes about, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken casually, 'rushin'' sounds like the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Yeltsin was the first president of the Russian Federation, so his compatriots are citizens of that country.

clue.text: Involve unavoidably in tale unfolding

indicators.note: unfolding suggests the words are opened out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A story whose plot gets someone necessarily caught up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfolding' rearranges the letters of IN and TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to have as a necessary consequence, so to require or involve.

clue.text: Matt may hesitate which is even more boring

parts.note: matt describes a finish that is dull, not glossy
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A man named Matt hums and haws, making him tedious company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matt' looks like a man's name but is the unshiny paint finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Duller is the comparative of dull, meaning more tedious.

clue.text: Debate as to which fuel is to be used?

definitions.text: Debate as to which fuel is to be used?

parts.words: Debate as to which fuel is to be used?
parts.note: read literally, a dispute over what to put on the fire; the phrase really means a hotly discussed matter

explanation.surface: An argument about whether to burn coal or wood.
explanation.definitionFit: An urgent and hotly debated issue, here pictured as a question about what to set alight.

clue.text: Primate, right he's from America

parts.note: taken as written, dropping the apostrophe
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: Someone confirms a monkey is from the New World.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus is a macaque monkey from South Asia, a primate used in research.

clue.text: Scramble to join an eastern religion

parts.note: to shin is to climb or scramble up something
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rush to sign up for an Asian faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scramble' looks like an anagram signal, but it is SHIN, to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the indigenous religion of Japan, worshipping kami spirits.

clue.text: Brave nurse helped prisoners call round 8th May

indicators.note: round means the call word is placed around the date

parts.note: 8 May 1945 was VE Day, Victory in Europe

explanation.surface: A heroic nurse who aided captives telephoned around the date of victory.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Cavell was a British nurse executed in 1915 for helping Allied soldiers escape occupied Belgium. 8 May is VE (Victory in Europe) Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Cavell, the British wartime nurse, was shot by the Germans for helping Allied soldiers escape.

clue.text: Short, close-fitting wear athlete Seb ate in

indicators.note: in means the eating word goes inside the athlete's surname

parts.note: Sebastian Coe is the British Olympic middle-distance runner
taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous runner wearing a snug jacket had a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Seb Coe is a British Olympic champion runner, later Lord Coe.
explanation.definitionFit: A coatee is a short tight-fitting coat or jacket.

clue.text: Mum taking girl on the river

parts.note: mum as in keep mum, be quiet, which is sh
Ann is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother brings her daughter along on a boat trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but silence, as in 'mum's the word'. The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is Ireland's longest river.

clue.text: Something afoot in the animal world!

definitions.text: Something afoot in the animal world!

parts.words: Something afoot in the animal world!
parts.note: afoot looks like happening, but read literally it is a beast's foot

explanation.surface: Something is going on among the wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: A horny foot of a horse or cow, literally a creature's foot.

clue.text: Highly placed at observation post

parts.note: taken as written
OP is the military abbreviation for observation post

explanation.surface: A lookout perched high at its station.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on the top of, so placed high up.

clue.text: Mark is found in girl friend's car

indicators.note: is found in says the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: A scratch turns up on a girlfriend's vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is found in' points to letters inside friend'S CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting mark left on the skin by a healed wound.

clue.text: Worker, one still not attracting dust

parts.note: a worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
one is the Roman numeral I
static means still, motionless

explanation.surface: A labourer stays motionless and gathers no dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: An antistatic coating stops a static charge building up, so dust is not drawn to the surface.

clue.text: Pastry that's swell

definitions.meaning: a light flaky pastry, as in a cream one

explanation.definitionFit: Puff pastry is light flaky dough, and to puff up is to swell or inflate.

clue.text: One retaining one end of the pitch?

definitions.text: One retaining one end of the pitch?

parts.words: One retaining one end of the pitch?
parts.note: read literally, a person holding on to a stretch of ground; really the player who guards the net

explanation.surface: Someone holding on to part of a sports field.
explanation.definitionFit: The player who guards the net at one end of a football field.
